<!-- source: README.md -->
# @sugatoray-ai/aiskills

`@sugatoray-ai/aiskills` installs Sugato Ray's agent skills (scrolls, stata, personas, newsletters, diagrams, docs, development) into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and every other agent the [`skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/skills) CLI supports.

The skills ship inside the npm package, are saved to `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/`, and are registered with your agents by `npx skills add`. The `aiskills` command then installs, lists and removes them by name, by group or by pattern, and with `--route` it manages skills from other sources too.

```bash
npm install -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills
```

That is all most people need: the install step registers every skill with the agents it finds. To choose a group and an agent yourself:

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -G scrolls -a claude-code
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] bundled: scrolls-help, scrolls-hide, scrolls-remove, scrolls-restore, scrolls-setup, scrolls-unhide, scrolls-update
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills --global --skill scrolls-help --skill scrolls-hide --skill scrolls-remove --skill scrolls-restore --skill scrolls-setup --skill scrolls-unhide --skill scrolls-update --agent claude-code --yes
```

`npx skills` then prints its own progress and installs the seven skills for Claude Code.

## Features

- **Every skill in one package**: 13 skills in 6 groups, at the version you installed.
- **Install on `npm install -g`**: a `postinstall` step saves and registers the skills, and never fails the npm install.
- **Pick what you want**: by skill (`-s`), by group (`-G scrolls`), by agent (`-a codex`), with glob patterns (`-s 'scrolls-*'`).
- **Global or per project**: `-g` (default) or `-p`.
- **Clean uninstall**: full, partial, per agent or per project, with `--dry-run` and `--purge`.
- **External skills too**: `--route` (or the `aix` command) looks up and installs skills that aren't bundled.
- **Two layouts**: flat (one folder per skill) or `--nested` (the repo's own folders).
- **Short commands**: `ais` is `aiskills`; `aix` is `aiskills --route`; `i`, `r`, `ls`, `g`, `f`, `p`, `h` are aliases.
- **Safe by default**: a pinned `skills` CLI, checked registry results, and no runtime dependencies.

<!-- source: getting-started/why-aiskills.md -->
# Why aiskills

`aiskills` gives you Sugato Ray's skills as one versioned npm package, and lets you install them by group or pattern instead of one by one.

The [`skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/skills) CLI (`npx skills`) already installs agent skills from GitHub, URLs and local folders into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and many other agents. `aiskills` doesn't replace it. It sits on top of it and adds what `npx skills` doesn't know about this collection of skills.

## What it adds

| You want to | With `npx skills` alone | With `aiskills` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Get all the skills | `npx skills add sugatoray/aiskills --global` (latest `master`) | `npm install -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills` (a released, versioned set) |
| Install a related set | List each skill with `--skill` | `-G scrolls` (groups come from the repo's `marketplace.json`) |
| Pick by pattern | Not supported | `-s 'scrolls-*'`, `-a 'claude*'` |
| Remove only these skills | Name each one; same-named skills from other sources go too | `aiskills uninstall` removes exactly what it installed |
| Work offline after install | Needs GitHub for each add | Skills are already on disk in `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills` |
| Install other people's skills too | Yes | Yes, with `--route` or `aix` |

## When you don't need it

- You want only one or two skills and don't mind naming them: `npx skills add sugatoray/aiskills --skill <name> --global` is enough.
- You want skills that track the repo's `master` branch, not releases.
- You install skills only per project from `node_modules`: then you need the package, but not the `aiskills` command. See [Use the package with `npx skills experimental_sync`](../guides/use-experimental-sync.md).

## What it doesn't do

- It doesn't copy skills into agent folders itself. `npx skills` does that, and keeps its own record of what is installed.
- It doesn't install Claude Code plugins. It reads the repo's `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` only to group the skills.
- It doesn't update skills by itself. Install a newer package version (`npm install -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills@latest`) to get newer skills.

See also: [How aiskills works](../concepts/how-it-works.md) · [Installation](installation.md)

<!-- source: getting-started/installation.md -->
# Installation

Install the package globally with npm; its install step saves the skills and registers them with your agents.

**You'll need:** Node.js 18.17 or newer, and npm. `npx` (which comes with npm) must be able to reach the npm registry the first time it downloads the `skills` CLI.

## Install

```bash
npm install -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills
```

npm runs the package's `postinstall` step, which:

1. saves the skills to `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/`, replacing any older copy, and
2. runs `npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills --global --skill '*' --yes`, which installs every skill for every agent `npx skills` detects.

npm 7 and later hide the output of install steps, so you won't see this happen. If step 2 fails (offline, behind a proxy, or with `--ignore-scripts`), the npm install still succeeds. Run it again with `aiskills install`.

> [!NOTE]
> pnpm and bun don't run install steps by default. After `pnpm add -g` or `bun add -g`, run `aiskills install` once.

## Choose what the install step does

The install step reads `AISKILLS_*` environment variables. For example, only the scrolls group, only for Claude Code:

```bash
AISKILLS_GROUPS=scrolls AISKILLS_AGENTS=claude-code npm install -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills
```

To save the files but not register them, set `AISKILLS_SKIP_SKILLS_ADD=1`. To skip the step entirely, set `AISKILLS_SKIP_POSTINSTALL=1`. All the variables are in [Configure the npm install step](../guides/configure-npm-install.md).

## Check it worked

The package adds three commands: `aiskills`, `ais` (the same, shorter) and `aix` (the same as `aiskills --route`).

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills --version
aiskills path
```

```text
0.3.0
~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills
```

`aiskills installed` lists the skills that `npx skills` has recorded as installed from that folder. See [Quickstart](quickstart.md).

## Without a global install

`npx` runs the package's `aiskills` command without a global install:

```bash
npx @sugatoray-ai/aiskills install -G scrolls
```

## Update

Install the newer version the same way. The install step replaces `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/` with the new skills and runs `npx skills add` again:

```bash
npm install -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills@latest
```

If you had chosen particular skills, agents or flags, run that `aiskills install ...` command again afterwards (or set the same `AISKILLS_*` variables for the npm install).

## Remove

npm doesn't run any step on uninstall, so remove the skills first:

```bash
aiskills uninstall --purge
npm uninstall -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills
```

See [Remove everything](../guides/remove-everything.md).

See also: [Quickstart](quickstart.md) · [Environment variables](../reference/environment.md)

<!-- source: getting-started/quickstart.md -->
# Quickstart

In five commands: see what's in the package, install a group for one agent, check it, and remove it.

**You'll need:** the package installed ([Installation](installation.md)).

## 1. See the groups

```bash
aiskills groups
```

Each group lists its alias and its skills. The full output is in [Tutorial step 1](../tutorial/01-install-a-group.md).

## 2. Install a group for one agent

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -G personas -a claude-code
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] bundled: prodigy
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills --global --skill prodigy --agent claude-code --yes
```

`npx skills` then prints its own progress. In Claude Code, the skill is now available as `/prodigy`.

## 3. Check what's installed

<!-- verify: list=prodigy -->
```bash
aiskills installed
```

```text
prodigy                    personas-skills        Claude Code
```

The columns are the skill, its group, and the agents it is installed for.

## 4. Preview the removal

<!-- verify: list=prodigy -->
```bash
aiskills uninstall -n
```

```text
[aiskills] [dry-run] would remove (global): prodigy
[aiskills] [dry-run] npx -y skills@1.7.6 remove prodigy --global --yes
[aiskills] skill files kept in ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (re-add with 'aiskills install'; delete with --purge).
```

## 5. Remove it

```bash
aiskills uninstall
```

As the preview said, the skill files stay in `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/`, so `aiskills install` can add them back offline.

## Recap

- `aiskills groups` shows what you can install.
- `aiskills install -G <group> -a <agent>` installs a group for an agent.
- `aiskills installed` and `aiskills uninstall -n` show what is there and what would go.

Next: the [Tutorial](../tutorial/01-install-a-group.md) covers patterns, projects, external skills and uninstalling in more depth.

See also: [CLI reference](../reference/cli.md)

<!-- source: skills/create-issues-update-pr.md -->
# create-issues-update-pr

Files GitHub issue(s) for work already done (or about to be done) on a branch/PR, grouping related issues under a parent epic when there's a genuine hierarchy — using GitHub's native parent/child issue relationship, not just labels — and then updates that pull request's title (kept short) and description so the description lists every issue in the exact format '- Closes #{{issue-number}} -- {{issue-title}}', indented to match parent-child nesting. Use this whenever the user asks to file issue(s) for a PR, 'add gh issues for this', 'track this as issues', link a PR to tracking issues, or update a PR's title/description to list the issues covering its changes — including when they invoke /create-issues-update-pr directly. Also trigger when a PR description is stale or generic relative to its actual current commits and the user wants it brought up to date alongside issue creation.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Group | `repo-related-skills` (alias `repo-related`) |
| Version | 1.3.0 |
| Starts | When you type `/create-issues-update-pr`, or your agent uses it when a task fits its description |
| Needs | GitHub MCP server tools with write access to the target repository: issue_write, sub_issue_write, list_issue_types, search_issues/list_issues, pull_request_read, update_pull_request. Works against any GitHub repository the current session has push/write access to, not just this one. |
| License | MIT |
| Source | [skills/development/repo-related/create-issues-update-pr](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/tree/master/skills/development/repo-related/create-issues-update-pr) |

## Install

For one agent (leave out `-a` for every agent `npx skills` finds):

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -s create-issues-update-pr -a claude-code
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] bundled: create-issues-update-pr
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills --global --skill create-issues-update-pr --agent claude-code --yes
```

Or the whole `repo-related-skills` group:

```bash
aiskills install -G repo-related -a claude-code
```

Into the current project instead: add `-p`. To remove it:

```bash
aiskills uninstall -s create-issues-update-pr
```

## What's inside

The files that ship with the skill, in `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/create-issues-update-pr/`:

- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`
- `CHANGELOG.md`
- `README.md`
- `SKILL.md`
- `agents/claude-code.yaml`
- `agents/openai.yaml`
- `meta/MAINTAINERS.md`

See also: [All skills](README.md) · [README](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/blob/master/skills/development/repo-related/create-issues-update-pr/README.md) · [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/blob/master/skills/development/repo-related/create-issues-update-pr/CHANGELOG.md) · [Skill groups](../concepts/skill-groups.md)

<!-- source: skills/create-lib-docs.md -->
# create-lib-docs

Writes top-grade, verified user documentation for a library, CLI or framework as a folder of Markdown pages plus SVG diagrams, structured the way FastAPI, Pydantic, DuckDB and Effect structure theirs: a landing page with a 30-second example, Getting Started, a progressive Tutorial with runnable steps, task-oriented How-to Guides, Concepts (explanations with diagrams), an exhaustive Reference (CLI flags, API, config, output schemas, one anchor per error with cause and fix), FAQ/troubleshooting, and llms.txt / llms-full.txt so AI agents can load the docs. Every fact is taken from the code, --help output and tests (never from memory), and every snippet is run before it is published. Use this whenever the user asks to write, create, restructure or overhaul documentation / docs / a user guide / a manual / API reference for a library, package, CLI or framework, wants docs 'like FastAPI's / Pydantic's / DuckDB's / Effect's', wants docs that help both humans and AI agents, or invokes /create-lib-docs.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Group | `docs-skills` (alias `docs`) |
| Version | 1.1.0 |
| Starts | When you ask for it: you type `/create-lib-docs` (your agent doesn't start it on its own) |
| License | MIT |
| Source | [skills/docs/create-lib-docs](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/tree/master/skills/docs/create-lib-docs) |

## Install

For one agent (leave out `-a` for every agent `npx skills` finds):

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -s create-lib-docs -a claude-code
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] bundled: create-lib-docs
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills --global --skill create-lib-docs --agent claude-code --yes
```

Or the whole `docs-skills` group:

```bash
aiskills install -G docs -a claude-code
```

Into the current project instead: add `-p`. To remove it:

```bash
aiskills uninstall -s create-lib-docs
```

## What's inside

The files that ship with the skill, in `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/create-lib-docs/`:

- `CHANGELOG.md`
- `README.md`
- `SKILL.md`
- `agents/openai.yaml`
- `meta/MAINTAINERS.md`
- `references/patterns.md`
- `references/templates.md`
- `scripts/build_llms_txt.py`
- `scripts/check_docs.py`
- `tests/test_scripts.py`

See also: [All skills](README.md) · [README](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/blob/master/skills/docs/create-lib-docs/README.md) · [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/blob/master/skills/docs/create-lib-docs/CHANGELOG.md) · [Skill groups](../concepts/skill-groups.md)

<!-- source: skills/network-flow.md -->
# network-flow

Create working interactive network and architecture diagrams with moving packets, orthogonal connections, scenario playback, and selectable nodes. Use when the user invokes /network-flow or asks for live flowing diagrams, animated system architecture, request flows, RAG pipelines, or agent workflow visualizations. Accept descriptions, reference images, source material, or graph JSON. Deliver a self-contained HTML file with a working preview when supported; complete rendering, browser verification, and file delivery rather than stopping at a diagram description.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Group | `diagrams-skills` (alias `diagrams`) |
| Version | 1.0.0 |
| Starts | When you ask for it: you type `/network-flow` (your agent doesn't start it on its own) |
| Needs | Python 3.9+ (stdlib only) for validation and HTML generation; modern browser with SVG and ResizeObserver for playback; optional Node.js and Playwright for browser checks |
| License | MIT |
| Source | [skills/diagrams/network-flow](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/tree/master/skills/diagrams/network-flow) |

## Install

For one agent (leave out `-a` for every agent `npx skills` finds):

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -s network-flow -a claude-code
```



```bash

```

# newsletter-ai

Generates the weekly executive AI intelligence newsletter: researches the last 7 days of AI developments (with 30-90 day context where needed) and writes them up as a 15-part executive brief — the Top 20 developments, model intelligence, open-vs-closed, talent, funding/M&A, production deployment, agents, chips/compute, data centers/energy, the global AI race, a company watchlist, key numbers, under-the-radar signals, what changed this week, and a closing synthesis. Defaults to markdown chat output; pass -o/--output yaml (or --yaml) to instead produce a sourced YAML document, and add -r/--report path/to/folder-or-report.html to render it straight into an interactive, light/dark, multi-tab HTML report (with per-tab References accordions, its source YAML fused in for single-file distribution, and a Download-data button) written next to a copy of the YAML. Use when the user runs /newsletter-ai (aliased as the shorthand /nltr-ai — treat both identically), or asks to draft, write, or update this week's AI newsletter/intelligence brief.

# prodigy

Act as the top performer in a given role or field and produce a five-part playbook: (1) how they understand the problem, constraints, stakeholders and success metrics; (2) how they design, break down and deliver a solution, including iteration, validation and communication; (3) the biggest pitfalls and how they avoid them; (4) a short set of operating principles and decision rules; (5) a practical learning plan with daily habits, projects and feedback loops for someone to level up. Use when the user invokes /prodigy, optionally with a role or field (e.g. /prodigy product manager, /prodigy SRE, /prodigy negotiation), or asks how the best person in a role thinks and works.

# scrolls-help

Shows a crisp, example-driven reference for the whole scrolls skill family (/scrolls-setup, /scrolls-update, /scrolls-hide, /scrolls-unhide, /scrolls-remove, /scrolls-restore) — what each command does, their shared -p/-t/-l/-r/-u/-x/--onto flags, and common usage examples (new project, monorepo, running from a subdirectory, toggling hidden/visible, removing and restoring scrolls). Use this whenever the user runs /scrolls-help, or asks what the scrolls commands do, how to use them, what flags they take, which one they need, or seems unsure about docs/.scrolls setup — even if they only name one of the six commands rather than 'scrolls' generally. Supports -e/--online to render it as a styled page served on an OS-assigned localhost port instead of chat text, with light/dark and colorize/plain toggles. Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows (bash or PowerShell).

<!-- source: skills/scrolls-hide.md -->
# scrolls-hide

Converts an already-set-up docs/scrolls/ working-memory folder from visible (scrolls) to dotfile-hidden (.scrolls), renaming the folder and rewriting the path references inside it and in SCROLLS.md so nothing breaks. Use this whenever the user runs /scrolls-hide, or asks to hide, dot, or re-hide the scrolls folder, go back to hiding project memory / docs/.scrolls, or rename scrolls to .scrolls. This is the retrofit path for a project that was set up visible and now wants it hidden — for a brand-new project, /scrolls-setup's default (no -u/--unhide flag) already creates it hidden and this skill isn't needed. By default checks one exact location (docs/scrolls under the current directory); supports -r/--recurse to sweep an entire directory tree instead (e.g. every package in a monorepo in one run), repeatable -p/--path to target specific locations, -t/--reporoot to target the git repository's top level regardless of which subdirectory you're in, -l/--local to target the current directory explicitly, and the DEFAULT_SCROLLS_RELPATH environment variable to change the default location. Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows (bash or PowerShell). The opposite of /scrolls-unhide.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Group | `scrolls-skills` (alias `scrolls`) |
| Version | 2.4.0 |
| Starts | When you ask for it: you type `/scrolls-hide` (your agent doesn't start it on its own) |
| Needs | bash (macOS/Linux/WSL) or PowerShell 7+ (pwsh) or PowerShell (older versions: powershell.exe); Python 3.9+ (stdlib only, no dependencies) |
| License | MIT |
| Source | [skills/scrolls/scrolls-hide](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/tree/master/skills/scrolls/scrolls-hide) |

<!-- source: skills/scrolls-remove.md -->
# scrolls-remove

Removes a docs/.scrolls/ (or docs/scrolls/) project-memory system from a git repository — the exact opposite of /scrolls-setup. Deletes the scrolls folder, deletes SCROLLS.md, strips the scrolls pointer stub out of CLAUDE.md (and the dangling pointer out of AGENTS.md), deleting either file outright only when nothing else is left in it, and records the whole removal as ONE git commit whose message names the commit just before the removal, so it can always be undone. Use this whenever the user runs /scrolls-remove, or asks to remove, delete, uninstall, tear down, or get rid of the scrolls / project memory / docs/.scrolls. Supports -p/--path (repeatable), -t/--reporoot, -l/--local, -r/--recurse to find and remove every scrolls folder under a directory in one commit, -x/--purge [CLAUDE.md|AGENTS.md|SCROLLS.md|<other file>|all] to delete pointer files outright even when they hold other content, -n/--dry-run, -y/--yes to skip the confirmation, and --no-commit. Refuses to run when anything it would remove has uncommitted changes, since those could not be restored. Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows (bash or PowerShell).

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Group | `scrolls-skills` (alias `scrolls`) |
| Version | 2.4.0 |
| Starts | When you ask for it: you type `/scrolls-remove` (your agent doesn't start it on its own) |
| Needs | bash (macOS/Linux/WSL) or PowerShell 7+ (pwsh) or PowerShell (older versions: powershell.exe); Python 3.9+ (stdlib only, no dependencies); git |
| License | MIT |
| Source | [skills/scrolls/scrolls-remove](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/tree/master/skills/scrolls/scrolls-remove) |

<!-- source: skills/scrolls-restore.md -->
# scrolls-restore

Restores a docs/.scrolls/ (or docs/scrolls/) project-memory system from git history — the counterpart to /scrolls-remove. By default finds the newest /scrolls-remove checkpoint in HEAD's history and brings back exactly what it removed; or takes any COMMIT (a removal commit, or an ordinary commit containing a scrolls folder). Restores ONLY the agentic memory — the scrolls folders plus the SCROLLS.md/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md pointer stubs, re-inserted into those files as they are today — never rolling back anything else in the repository, and records it as one git commit. --onto REF mounts the memory onto another branch (or, with -b, a new branch at any commit) through a temporary worktree, without touching the current checkout. Use this whenever the user runs /scrolls-restore, or asks to restore, bring back, recover, undo the removal of, or re-mount the scrolls / project memory / docs/.scrolls. Supports -p/--path (repeatable), -t/--reporoot, -l/--local, -r/--recurse, --onto, -b/--branch, --full, -f/--force, --list [--all], -n/--dry-run, -y/--yes, and --no-commit. Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows (bash or PowerShell).

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Group | `scrolls-skills` (alias `scrolls`) |
| Version | 2.4.0 |
| Starts | When you ask for it: you type `/scrolls-restore` (your agent doesn't start it on its own) |
| Needs | bash (macOS/Linux/WSL) or PowerShell 7+ (pwsh) or PowerShell (older versions: powershell.exe); Python 3.9+ (stdlib only, no dependencies); git |
| License | MIT |
| Source | [skills/scrolls/scrolls-restore](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/tree/master/skills/scrolls/scrolls-restore) |

<!-- source: skills/scrolls-setup.md -->
# scrolls-setup

Sets up a minimal docs/.scrolls/ working-memory system for a project — a small set of cross-session memory files (STARTER.md, SPEC.md, HANDOFF.md, GAP_ANALYSIS.md, GAP_CONTEXT.md, PLAN.md, WISDOM.md) plus a SCROLLS.md file that points future sessions at STARTER.md, a short CLAUDE.md pointer to SCROLLS.md, and a matching AGENTS.md pointer to CLAUDE.md for other agent harnesses. Use this whenever the user runs /scrolls-setup, or asks to set up 'scrolls', a project-memory system, session handoff notes, a docs/.scrolls folder, or a CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/SCROLLS.md that points new sessions at persistent project docs. Trigger even if the project has no docs/ folder, no CLAUDE.md, no AGENTS.md, or no SCROLLS.md yet — creating them is part of the job. Supports -p/--path for a custom docs location, -t/--reporoot to pin everything to the git repository's top level regardless of which subdirectory you're in, -l/--local to pin it explicitly to the current directory, -r/--recurse to scan recursively for an existing scrolls folder before creating a new one (avoiding accidental duplicates), and -u/--unhide to name the folder scrolls instead of .scrolls. Defaults to the current directory, but warns first if that differs from the repo root so a subdirectory invocation doesn't silently create a second, disconnected scrolls system. Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows (bash or PowerShell).

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Group | `scrolls-skills` (alias `scrolls`) |
| Version | 2.4.0 |
| Starts | When you ask for it: you type `/scrolls-setup` (your agent doesn't start it on its own) |
| Needs | bash (macOS/Linux/WSL) or PowerShell 7+ (pwsh) or PowerShell (older versions: powershell.exe); Python 3.9+ (stdlib only, no dependencies) |
| License | MIT |
| Source | [skills/scrolls/scrolls-setup](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/tree/master/skills/scrolls/scrolls-setup) |

<!-- source: skills/scrolls-unhide.md -->
# scrolls-unhide

Converts an already-set-up docs/.scrolls/ working-memory folder from dotfile-hidden (.scrolls) to visible (scrolls), renaming the folder and rewriting the path references inside it and in SCROLLS.md so nothing breaks. Use this whenever the user runs /scrolls-unhide, or asks to unhide, un-dot, or show the scrolls folder, stop hiding project memory / docs/.scrolls, or rename .scrolls to scrolls. This is the retrofit path for a project that was set up hidden and now wants it visible — for a brand-new project, /scrolls-setup's own -u/--unhide flag does this in one step and this skill isn't needed. By default checks one exact location (docs/.scrolls under the current directory); supports -r/--recurse to sweep an entire directory tree instead (e.g. every package in a monorepo in one run), repeatable -p/--path to target specific locations, -t/--reporoot to target the git repository's top level regardless of which subdirectory you're in, -l/--local to target the current directory explicitly, and the DEFAULT_SCROLLS_RELPATH environment variable to change the default location. Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows (bash or PowerShell). The opposite of /scrolls-hide.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Group | `scrolls-skills` (alias `scrolls`) |
| Version | 2.4.0 |
| Starts | When you ask for it: you type `/scrolls-unhide` (your agent doesn't start it on its own) |
| Needs | bash (macOS/Linux/WSL) or PowerShell 7+ (pwsh) or PowerShell (older versions: powershell.exe); Python 3.9+ (stdlib only, no dependencies) |
| License | MIT |
| Source | [skills/scrolls/scrolls-unhide](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/tree/master/skills/scrolls/scrolls-unhide) |

## Install

For one agent (leave out `-a` for every agent `npx skills` finds):

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -s scrolls-unhide -a claude-code
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] bundled: scrolls-unhide
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills --global --skill scrolls-unhide --agent claude-code --yes
```

Or the whole `scrolls-skills` group:

```bash
aiskills install -G scrolls -a claude-code
```

Into the current project instead: add `-p`. To remove it:

```bash
aiskills uninstall -s scrolls-unhide
```

## What's inside

The files that ship with the skill, in `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/scrolls-unhide/`:

- `CHANGELOG.md`
- `README.md`
- `SKILL.md`
- `agents/openai.yaml`
- `assets/EXAMPLES.md`
- `meta/MAINTAINERS.md`
- `scripts/unhide.ps1`
- `scripts/unhide.sh`
- `tests/test_unhide.ps1`
- `tests/test_unhide.sh`

See also: [All skills](README.md) · [README](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/blob/master/skills/scrolls/scrolls-unhide/README.md) · [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/blob/master/skills/scrolls/scrolls-unhide/CHANGELOG.md) · [Skill groups](../concepts/skill-groups.md)

<!-- source: skills/scrolls-update.md -->
# scrolls-update

Updates an existing docs/.scrolls/ project-memory system (STARTER.md, SPEC.md, HANDOFF.md, GAP_ANALYSIS.md, GAP_CONTEXT.md, PLAN.md, WISDOM.md, and any project-specific scrolls beyond that core set) to reflect what actually happened in the current session, following each file's own update rule instead of appending blindly. Also backfills SCROLLS.md/CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md if the project predates them (idempotent — safe every run, never overwrites existing CLAUDE.md content). Use this whenever the user runs /scrolls-update, or asks to update the scrolls, refresh HANDOFF.md, write session handoff notes, record what was just done, close out or wrap up a session, log a new gap or trap, or update project memory / STARTER.md's docs. This is the counterpart to /scrolls-setup (which creates the system once) — use this one for every session afterward. Supports -p/--path for a custom docs location, -t/--reporoot to look under the git repository's top level regardless of which subdirectory you're in, -l/--local to look explicitly in the current directory, and -r/--recurse to search recursively for the scrolls folder if it isn't at the obvious exact location. Defaults to the current directory, but warns first if that differs from the repo root so a subdirectory invocation doesn't silently miss the real scrolls. Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows (bash or PowerShell). If no scrolls folder is found, say so and point at /scrolls-setup instead of inventing files here.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Group | `scrolls-skills` (alias `scrolls`) |
| Version | 2.4.0 |
| Starts | When you ask for it: you type `/scrolls-update` (your agent doesn't start it on its own) |
| Needs | bash (macOS/Linux/WSL) or PowerShell 7+ (pwsh) or PowerShell (older versions: powershell.exe); Python 3.9+ (stdlib only, no dependencies) |
| License | MIT |
| Source | [skills/scrolls/scrolls-update](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/tree/master/skills/scrolls/scrolls-update) |

## Install

For one agent (leave out `-a` for every agent `npx skills` finds):

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -s scrolls-update -a claude-code
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] bundled: scrolls-update
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills --global --skill scrolls-update --agent claude-code --yes
```

Or the whole `scrolls-skills` group:

```bash
aiskills install -G scrolls -a claude-code
```

Into the current project instead: add `-p`. To remove it:

```bash
aiskills uninstall -s scrolls-update
```

## What's inside

The files that ship with the skill, in `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/scrolls-update/`:

- `CHANGELOG.md`
- `README.md`
- `SKILL.md`
- `agents/openai.yaml`
- `assets/EXAMPLES.md`
- `meta/MAINTAINERS.md`
- `scripts/session_diff.ps1`
- `scripts/session_diff.sh`
- `tests/test_session_diff.ps1`
- `tests/test_session_diff.sh`

See also: [All skills](README.md) · [README](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/blob/master/skills/scrolls/scrolls-update/README.md) · [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/blob/master/skills/scrolls/scrolls-update/CHANGELOG.md) · [Skill groups](../concepts/skill-groups.md)

<!-- source: skills/stata-recipes.md -->
# stata-recipes

Turns a plain-language description of a data/statistics task into correct, runnable Stata code — a .do file or command sequence, not pseudocode. Use this whenever the user asks how to do something in Stata, wants a Stata command or .do file written or fixed, mentions Stata alongside a modeling task (regression, panel data, time series, ARDL, fixed effects, diff-in-diff, matching, etc.), or wants Stata and Python working together (running Python from inside a .do file, pulling Stata's dataset into pandas, or driving Stata from a Python script via pystata/stata_setup or batch mode). Also trigger when the user pastes Stata code that errors or gives wrong-looking results and wants it debugged, or asks 'is this good Stata style' / 'what's wrong with this command'. Covers a growing library of named recipes for common econometric workflows (ARDL modeling shipped now; more added over time) that produce a ready-to-run script, not just an explanation.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Group | `stata-skills` (alias `stata`) |
| Version | 1.3.2 |
| Starts | When you type `/stata-recipes`, or your agent uses it when a task fits its description |
| Needs | Stata 16+ (Stata 17+ recommended — modern `ardl` command and built-in Python integration); optionally Python 3.9+ with the `pystata`/`stata_setup` package (bundled with Stata 17+) for Stata<->Python interop |
| License | MIT |
| Source | [skills/stata/stata-recipes](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills/tree/master/skills/stata/stata-recipes) |

## Install

For one agent (leave out `-a` for every agent `npx skills` finds):


<!-- source: tutorial/01-install-a-group.md -->
# 1. Install a group

After this step you can find a group of skills and install it for one agent.

**You'll need:** the package installed ([Installation](../getting-started/installation.md)), and at least one agent that `npx skills` supports, such as Claude Code.

## See the groups

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills groups
```

```text
scrolls-skills  (alias: scrolls)
  Scrolls: a git-native markdown system for agentic memory that persists project state across sessions and ag...
  skills: scrolls-help, scrolls-hide, scrolls-remove, scrolls-restore, scrolls-setup, scrolls-unhide, scrolls-update

stata-skills  (alias: stata)
  Stata skills: turns a plain-language data/statistics task into correct, runnable Stata code, with good-vs-b...
  skills: stata-recipes

repo-related-skills  (alias: repo-related)
  Repo-related skills: acting on a repository's own hosted state (issues, pull requests, releases, and simila...
  skills: create-issues-update-pr

docs-skills  (alias: docs)
  Docs skills: writes verified user documentation for a library, CLI or framework, structured like FastAPI, P...
  skills: create-lib-docs

diagrams-skills  (alias: diagrams)
  Animated architecture and network diagrams with flowing packets, orthogonal routing, selectable nodes, and ...
  skills: network-flow

personas-skills  (alias: personas)
  Persona skills: /prodigy acts as the top performer in any role or field and shares how they frame problems,...
  skills: prodigy

(ungrouped; use -s or -G all)
  skills: newsletter-ai

Install a group:  aiskills install --group <name|alias> --global --agent <agent>
```

Each group has a name (`scrolls-skills`) and a shorter alias (`scrolls`, the name without `-skills`). Either works. `newsletter-ai` belongs to no group; you install it by name, or with the built-in group `all`.

## Install one group for one agent

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install --group scrolls --agent claude-code
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] bundled: scrolls-help, scrolls-hide, scrolls-remove, scrolls-restore, scrolls-setup, scrolls-unhide, scrolls-update
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills --global --skill scrolls-help --skill scrolls-hide --skill scrolls-remove --skill scrolls-restore --skill scrolls-setup --skill scrolls-unhide --skill scrolls-update --agent claude-code --yes
```

What happened, in order:

1. `aiskills` refreshed the skill files in `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/` from the package.
2. It turned the group into its seven skills (`bundled: ...`).
3. It ran `npx skills add` on that folder with one `--skill` per skill and your agent. `--global` is the default scope, and `--yes` skips `npx skills`' prompts.

`npx skills` prints its own progress after that line, and the skills appear in Claude Code as `/scrolls-setup`, `/scrolls-update` and so on.

> [!TIP]
> The same command, shorter: `ais i -G scrolls -a claude-code`. `ais` is `aiskills`, `i` is `install`, and `-G`/`-a` are the short forms of `--group`/`--agent`.

## Install several groups

Separate groups with commas, or repeat `-G`:

```bash
aiskills install -G scrolls,personas -a claude-code
aiskills install -G scrolls -G personas -a claude-code
```

## Recap

- `aiskills groups` lists groups, their aliases and their skills.
- `aiskills install -G <group> -a <agent>` installs a group for one agent; `-G` takes the name or the alias.
- `aiskills` always refreshes the saved skills, then hands the install to `npx skills add`.

Reference: [`install`](../reference/cli.md#install) · [`-G`, `--group`](../reference/cli.md#-g---group---groups) · [Skill groups](../concepts/skill-groups.md)

Next: [2. Pick skills and agents](02-pick-skills-and-agents.md)

<!-- source: tutorial/02-pick-skills-and-agents.md -->
# 2. Pick skills and agents

After this step you can choose skills by name or pattern and install them for several agents at once.

**You'll need:** the previous step.

## Name the skills

`-s` (`--skill`) takes skill names, separated by commas:

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -s scrolls-setup,scrolls-update -a claude-code
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] bundled: scrolls-setup, scrolls-update
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills --global --skill scrolls-setup --skill scrolls-update --agent claude-code --yes
```

## Use a pattern

`-s`, `-G` and `-a` accept glob patterns: `*` for any text, `?` for one character, `[abc]` for one of a set. Quote them so your shell leaves them alone:

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -s 'scrolls-[hu]*' -a claude-code
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] bundled: scrolls-help, scrolls-hide, scrolls-unhide, scrolls-update
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills --global --skill scrolls-help --skill scrolls-hide --skill scrolls-unhide --skill scrolls-update --agent claude-code --yes
```

The `bundled:` line shows what the pattern matched, before anything is installed. A pattern that matches nothing stops the command:

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -s 'scroll-*'
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] no skill matches: scroll-*
  available: create-issues-update-pr, create-lib-docs, network-flow, newsletter-ai, prodigy, scrolls-help, scrolls-hide, scrolls-remove, scrolls-restore, scrolls-setup, scrolls-unhide, scrolls-update, stata-recipes
```

## Mix skills and groups

`-s` and `-G` add up. This installs the personas group plus one skill:

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -G personas -s newsletter-ai -a claude-code
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] bundled: newsletter-ai, prodigy
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills --global --skill newsletter-ai --skill prodigy --agent claude-code --yes
```

## Several agents

`-a` takes several agents, and patterns too. Plain agent names are passed to `npx skills`, which checks them. A pattern is expanded against the agent list that `npx skills` itself reports, and the result is printed:

```bash
aiskills install -G stata -a claude-code,codex
aiskills install -G stata -a 'claude*,codex'
```

Leave out `-a` and `npx skills` installs for every agent it detects on your machine.

## Recap

- `-s` picks skills, `-G` picks groups, and they combine.
- Patterns work in `-s`, `-G` and `-a`; quote them.
- The `bundled:` line shows exactly what will be installed.

Reference: [`-s`, `--skill`](../reference/cli.md#-s---skill) · [`-a`, `--agent`](../reference/cli.md#-a---agent) · [Patterns](../reference/patterns.md)

Next: [3. Install into a project](03-install-into-a-project.md) · Previous: [1. Install a group](01-install-a-group.md)

<!-- source: tutorial/03-install-into-a-project.md -->
# 3. Install into a project

After this step you can install skills for one project only, so they travel with that project instead of applying to every project you open.

**You'll need:** the previous steps, and a project folder.

## Install with `-p`

Run the command from the project's folder and add `-p` (`--project`):

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -p -G stata -a claude-code
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] bundled: stata-recipes
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills --skill stata-recipes --agent claude-code --yes
```

Compare it with the global install in step 1: the command has no `--global`, and `aiskills` runs it from your current folder. `npx skills` then installs the skill into that project's agent folders (for Claude Code, `.claude/skills/`) and records it there.

The skill's source is still `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills`, so `aiskills` can recognise it later.

## List and remove project skills

`installed` and `uninstall` take `-p` too, and look at the current folder:

```bash
aiskills installed -p
aiskills uninstall -p -G stata
```

Global and project installs are separate. A skill can be installed in both, and removing one leaves the other.

## Set it at npm install time

To make the npm install step install into a project, set `AISKILLS_SCOPE=project` and run `npm install` in that project. The install step uses the folder npm was started from (`INIT_CWD`):

```bash
AISKILLS_SCOPE=project AISKILLS_GROUPS=stata npm install --save-dev @sugatoray-ai/aiskills
```

For a project dependency, [`npx skills experimental_sync`](../guides/use-experimental-sync.md) is another way to install the skills, pinned by your lockfile.

## Recap

- `-p` installs, lists and removes skills in the current project.
- The default, `-g`, is for your user, in every project.
- `AISKILLS_SCOPE=project` does the same for the npm install step.

Reference: [`-p`, `--project`](../reference/cli.md#-p---project) · [`AISKILLS_SCOPE`](../reference/environment.md#aiskills_scope)

Next: [4. Add external skills](04-add-external-skills.md) · Previous: [2. Pick skills and agents](02-pick-skills-and-agents.md)

<!-- source: tutorial/04-add-external-skills.md -->
# 4. Add external skills

After this step you can install skills that aren't in this package, from the skills registry or GitHub, with the same command.

**You'll need:** the previous steps, and network access to `skills.sh` and GitHub.

## Without `--route`, only bundled skills

`aiskills` refuses a skill name it doesn't bundle, before it installs anything:

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -s pdf
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] not provided by this package: pdf
  available: create-issues-update-pr, create-lib-docs, network-flow, newsletter-ai, prodigy, scrolls-help, scrolls-hide, scrolls-remove, scrolls-restore, scrolls-setup, scrolls-unhide, scrolls-update, stata-recipes
  add --route to look them up with 'npx skills' instead
```

## Look it up with `--route`

With `--route`, a bare name that isn't bundled is looked up with `npx skills find`. If exactly one result has exactly that name, it is installed:

<!-- verify: find=anthropics/skills@pdf -->
```bash
aiskills --route install -s pdf -a claude-code
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] 'pdf' is not bundled; looking it up with 'npx skills find pdf' ...
[aiskills] found anthropics/skills@pdf
[aiskills] external: anthropics/skills@pdf
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add anthropics/skills@pdf --global --agent claude-code --yes
```

The example output above was produced with a stand-in registry that returns one result, `anthropics/skills@pdf`; the real registry may return other results. If several results share the exact name, `aiskills` stops and lists them, and you pick one. It never chooses for you.

`aix` is a shorter way to write `aiskills --route`:

```bash
aix i -s pdf -a claude-code
```

## Name the source yourself

An `owner/repo@skill` (or `owner/repo`, a git URL, or a local path) skips the lookup and goes straight to `npx skills add`:

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aix install -s anthropics/skills@docx
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] external: anthropics/skills@docx
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add anthropics/skills@docx --global --yes
```

This is the safer choice for third-party skills: you decide exactly which source is used.

## Bundled and external together

`-s` can mix both, and `-G` still selects bundled groups. Every lookup runs before anything is installed, so a failed lookup changes nothing:

```bash
aix install -G scrolls -s pdf -a claude-code
```

## See both kinds

`installed --route` lists every installed skill with its source: `bundled` for this package's skills, otherwise the source `npx skills` recorded.

<!-- verify: list=scrolls-setup,anthropics/skills@docx -->
```bash
aix installed
```

```text
docx                       anthropics/skills              -                      Claude Code
scrolls-setup              bundled                        scrolls-skills         Claude Code
```

## Recap

- Without `--route`, `aiskills` only manages bundled skills.
- With `--route` (or `aix`), a bare name is looked up and installed only on a unique exact match; `owner/repo@skill` is used as given.
- External skills are installed from their source; they are never copied into `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills`.

Reference: [`--route`](../reference/cli.md#--route) · [Bundled and external skills](../concepts/bundled-and-external.md)

Next: [5. Uninstall](05-uninstall.md) · Previous: [3. Install into a project](03-install-into-a-project.md)

<!-- source: tutorial/05-uninstall.md -->
# 5. Uninstall

After this step you can remove some or all of the skills, and preview a removal first.

**You'll need:** the previous steps.

## Preview with `-n`

`-n` (`--dry-run`) prints what would be removed and the exact command, and changes nothing. Suppose `npx skills` has `scrolls-setup` and `prodigy` installed from this package, and `docx` from elsewhere:

<!-- verify: list=scrolls-setup,prodigy,anthropics/skills@docx -->
```bash
aiskills uninstall -n
```

```text
[aiskills] [dry-run] would remove (global): prodigy, scrolls-setup
[aiskills] [dry-run] npx -y skills@1.7.6 remove prodigy scrolls-setup --global --yes
[aiskills] skill files kept in ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (re-add with 'aiskills install'; delete with --purge).
```

A full uninstall removes only what `npx skills` recorded as installed from `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills`. `docx` isn't touched.

## Remove some skills

`-s` and `-G` work as they do for install, patterns included. With a pattern or a group, only skills that are actually installed are removed:

<!-- verify: list=scrolls-help,scrolls-hide,scrolls-setup -->
```bash
aiskills uninstall -s 'scrolls-[hu]*' -n
```

```text
[aiskills] [dry-run] would remove (global): scrolls-help, scrolls-hide
[aiskills] [dry-run] npx -y skills@1.7.6 remove scrolls-help scrolls-hide --global --yes
```

Drop `-n` to remove them:

```bash
aiskills uninstall -s 'scrolls-[hu]*'
```

## Remove from one agent

`-a` unlinks the skills from those agents only:

```bash
aiskills uninstall -a codex
```

## Remove an external skill

Without `--route`, `uninstall` refuses names this package doesn't provide. With it, names also match skills from other sources:

```bash
aix uninstall -s docx
```

## Remove everything, files included

`--purge` runs a full uninstall and then deletes `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills`:

<!-- verify: list=scrolls-setup -->
```bash
aiskills uninstall --purge -n
```

```text
[aiskills] [dry-run] would remove (global): scrolls-setup
[aiskills] [dry-run] npx -y skills@1.7.6 remove scrolls-setup --global --yes
[aiskills] [dry-run] would delete ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills
```

## Recap

- `-n` previews any uninstall.
- No `-s`/`-G` removes exactly what this package installed; `-s`/`-G`/`-a` narrow it.
- `--route` (or `aix`) lets names match skills from other sources.
- `--purge` also deletes the install folder.

Reference: [`uninstall`](../reference/cli.md#uninstall) · [Remove everything](../guides/remove-everything.md)

Previous: [4. Add external skills](04-add-external-skills.md) · Back to the [docs home](../README.md)

<!-- source: guides/configure-npm-install.md -->
# How to configure the npm install step

Use `AISKILLS_*` environment variables when you want `npm install` itself to install a particular set of skills, or nothing at all.

The package's `postinstall` step reads the same choices as `aiskills install`, but from the environment, because npm passes no arguments to it.

## Steps

1. Pick the variables for what you want:

   | You want | Set |
   | --- | --- |
   | Some groups | `AISKILLS_GROUPS=scrolls,personas` |
   | Some skills | `AISKILLS_SKILLS='scrolls-*,prodigy'` |
   | Some agents | `AISKILLS_AGENTS=claude-code,codex` |
   | The current project, not your user | `AISKILLS_SCOPE=project` |
   | Copies instead of symlinks | `AISKILLS_COPY=1` |
   | The repo's folder layout | `AISKILLS_LAYOUT=nested` |
   | Also external skills in `AISKILLS_SKILLS` | `AISKILLS_ROUTE=1` |

2. Set them on the npm command:

   ```bash
   AISKILLS_GROUPS=scrolls AISKILLS_AGENTS='claude*' npm install -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills
   ```

3. Check the result, since npm hides the step's output:

   ```bash
   aiskills installed
   ```

## Variations

### Save the files but don't register them

```bash
AISKILLS_SKIP_SKILLS_ADD=1 npm install -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills
```

The skills are saved to `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/`; run `aiskills install ...` later. The step also skips registering when `CI` is set.

### Skip the step entirely

```bash
AISKILLS_SKIP_POSTINSTALL=1 npm install -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills
```

Or `npm install --ignore-scripts`. Nothing is written until you run `aiskills install` or `aiskills sync`.

### Make the choices the defaults for the CLI too

`aiskills install`, `uninstall` and `installed` read the same variables as defaults; options on the command line replace them. Put them in your shell profile to use them everywhere:

```bash
export AISKILLS_AGENTS=claude-code,codex
```

## Troubleshooting

- **No skills appeared after `npm install`**: the step never fails the npm install, so look for a reason by running the same choice with the CLI, e.g. `aiskills install -G scrolls`. It prints the error.
- **pnpm or bun**: they skip install steps by default; run `aiskills install` once.
- **An unknown name in `AISKILLS_SKILLS`** stops the step with `unknown skill(s) in AISKILLS_SKILLS`. Fix the name, or set `AISKILLS_ROUTE=1` to look it up.

See also: [Environment variables](../reference/environment.md) · [Installation](../getting-started/installation.md)

<!-- source: guides/use-experimental-sync.md -->
# How to use the package with `npx skills experimental_sync`

Use this when you want a project's skills pinned by its lockfile, installed from `node_modules`, without the `aiskills` command or `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills`.

The `skills` CLI has an `experimental_sync` command that installs skills found in a project's `node_modules`. It looks for `<package>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, one level deep. This package ships its skills exactly that way.

## Steps

1. Add the package as a dev dependency, without its install step:

   ```bash
   npm install --save-dev --ignore-scripts @sugatoray-ai/aiskills
   ```

2. Install its skills into the project:

   ```bash
   npx skills experimental_sync --agent claude-code --yes
   ```

3. Commit the lockfile. Everyone who runs steps 1–2 gets the same skills.

## Variations

### Update

```bash
npm install --save-dev --ignore-scripts @sugatoray-ai/aiskills@latest
npx skills experimental_sync --agent claude-code --yes
```

## Troubleshooting

- **Nothing is installed**: check that `node_modules/@sugatoray-ai/aiskills/skills/` exists. It is created by `npm pack`, so it's there in the published package but not in a git checkout of the repo.
- **The command changed**: `experimental_sync` is marked experimental by the `skills` CLI and may change. `aiskills install -p` is the stable alternative.

See also: [Layouts: flat and nested](../concepts/layouts.md) · [3. Install into a project](../tutorial/03-install-into-a-project.md)

<!-- source: guides/keep-the-nested-layout.md -->
# How to keep the repo's nested layout

Use `--nested` when you want `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/` to look exactly like the repo's `skills/` folder, for browsing or editing.

## Steps

1. Rewrite the folder in the nested layout:

   <!-- verify -->
   ```bash
   aiskills sync --nested
   ```

   ```text
   [aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (nested layout)
   ```

2. Browse it: skills are now under their group folders, e.g. `skills/scrolls/scrolls-setup/`, with the groups' `README.md` and `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` files next to them.

The choice is saved in `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/aiskills.json`, so later `install`, `sync`, `list` and `groups` keep using it.

## Variations

### Install and nest in one go

```bash
aiskills --nested
aiskills install --nested -G scrolls
```

`aiskills --nested` on its own means `aiskills install --nested`.

### Go back to flat

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills sync --flat
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
```

### Nested from the npm install step

```bash
AISKILLS_LAYOUT=nested npm install -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills
```

## Troubleshooting

- **My edits disappeared**: every sync replaces `skills/`. Edit a copy elsewhere, or contribute the change to the repo.
- **Skills behave differently**: they don't; `npx skills add` finds the same skills in either layout.

See also: [Layouts: flat and nested](../concepts/layouts.md) · [`--nested`](../reference/cli.md#--nested)

<!-- source: guides/run-npx-skills-directly.md -->
# How to run any `npx skills` command

Use `aiskills skills <args>` when you need a `skills` command or flag that `aiskills` doesn't wrap, such as `update`, `use` or `init`.

It passes the arguments to `npx skills` unchanged, with two extras: the pinned `skills` version, and `:root` replaced by the install folder.

## Steps

1. Write the `npx skills` command you want, and put `aiskills skills` in front instead of `npx skills`:

   <!-- verify -->
   ```bash
   aiskills skills list -g
   ```

   ```text
   [aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 list -g
   ```

   The `npx skills` output follows that line.

2. Use `:root` where you need the install folder:

   <!-- verify -->
   ```bash
   aiskills skills add :root -s prodigy -g -y
   ```

   ```text
   [aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills -s prodigy -g -y
   ```

## Variations

### Extra flags on `install` and `uninstall`

Anything after `--` is added to the end of the `npx skills` command. For example, `--json` makes `npx skills add` print its result as JSON:

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills install -G stata -a claude-code -- --json
```

```text
[aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
[aiskills] bundled: stata-recipes
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 add ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills --global --skill stata-recipes --agent claude-code --yes --json
```

### Search the registry

`aiskills find <query>` is `npx skills find <query>`:

<!-- verify -->
```bash
aiskills find pdf
```

```text
[aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 find pdf
…
```

See also: [`skills`](../reference/cli.md#skills) · [Choose the `skills` CLI version](choose-the-skills-cli-version.md)

<!-- source: guides/remove-everything.md -->
# How to remove everything

Use this to take the skills, the install folder and the npm package off your machine.

npm runs nothing when a package is uninstalled, so remove the skills **before** the package.

## Steps

1. Preview:

   ```bash
   aiskills uninstall --purge -n
   ```

2. Remove every skill this package installed, then delete `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills`:

   ```bash
   aiskills uninstall --purge
   ```

3. If you installed into projects, repeat in each project:

   ```bash
   aiskills uninstall -p
   ```

4. Remove the package:

   ```bash
   npm uninstall -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills
   ```

## Variations

### The package is already gone

Run the CLI once through `npx`:

```bash
npx @sugatoray-ai/aiskills uninstall --purge
```

Or do it by hand with `npx skills`:

```bash
npx skills list -g
npx skills remove <skill...> --global --yes
rm -rf ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills
```

### External skills too

A full uninstall never removes skills from other sources, even with `--route`. Name them:

```bash
aix uninstall -s pdf,docx
```

## Troubleshooting

- **`--purge only applies to a full uninstall`**: drop `-s`/`-G`.
- **`... is not an aiskills folder ...`**: `AISKILLS_HOME` points at a folder that `aiskills` didn't create, so it refuses to delete it. See [Errors](../reference/errors.md#not-an-aiskills-folder).

See also: [5. Uninstall](../tutorial/05-uninstall.md) · [`--purge`](../reference/cli.md#--purge)

<!-- source: guides/use-from-an-agent.md -->
# How to use aiskills from an AI agent or a script

Use this page when a program, not a person, runs `aiskills`: an AI coding agent, a setup script, or CI.

## Steps

1. **Never wait for input.** `aiskills` never prompts, and it passes `--yes` to every `npx skills add` and `npx skills remove`. `npx -y` also skips npx's own download prompt.

2. **Check before you change.** Read the groups as JSON, and preview removals with `-n`:

   <!-- verify -->
   ```bash
   aiskills groups --json
   ```

   ```text
   {
     "groups": [
       {
         "name": "scrolls-skills",
         "alias": "scrolls",
   …
     "ungrouped": [
       "newsletter-ai"
     ]
   }
   ```

   The shape is `{ "groups": [{ "name", "alias", "description", "skills": [string] }], "ungrouped": [string] }`. See [Files and schemas](../reference/files.md#aiskills-groups---json).

3. **Install with explicit choices.** Name the skills or groups, the agents and the scope, so the result doesn't depend on what happens to be detected:

   ```bash
   aiskills install -g -G scrolls -a claude-code
   ```

4. **Branch on the exit code**, not on the text:

   | Exit code | Meaning |
   | --- | --- |
   | `0` | Success. For `uninstall`, also when there was nothing to remove. |
   | `1` | `aiskills` refused or failed: a bad option, an unknown name, a pattern that matched nothing, a failed lookup, an unsafe folder. No skill was installed or removed (the saved copy in `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills/` may have been refreshed). The message is on stderr and starts with `[aiskills]`. |
   | other | The exit code of `npx skills`, passed through. |

   <!-- verify -->
   ```bash
   aiskills install -G nope
   ```

   ```text
   [aiskills] skills saved to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/skills (flat layout)
   [aiskills] no group matches: nope
     available: scrolls-skills (scrolls), stata-skills (stata), repo-related-skills (repo-related), docs-skills (docs), diagrams-skills (diagrams), personas-skills (personas), all
     see 'aiskills groups'
   ```

   Every error is listed, with its cause and fix, in [Errors and exit codes](../reference/errors.md).

5. **Read what's installed as JSON** with the passthrough. `aiskills` prints one `[aiskills] running: ...` line before the JSON, so parse from the first `[` of the JSON array, or call `npx -y skills@1.7.6 list --json -g` yourself:

   <!-- verify -->
   ```bash
   aiskills skills list --json -g
   ```

   ```text
   [aiskills] running: npx -y skills@1.7.6 list --json -g
   []
   ```

   Each row has `name`, `source`, `sourceType`, `scope` and `agents`. A row with `sourceType` `local` and `source` equal to `aiskills path` was installed by `aiskills`. See [Files and schemas](../reference/files.md#npx-skills-list---json-rows).

## Variations

### Unattended install from npm

Set the choices as environment variables, so a single `npm install` does everything:

```bash
AISKILLS_GROUPS=scrolls AISKILLS_AGENTS=claude-code npm install -g @sugatoray-ai/aiskills
aiskills installed
```

The npm install step never fails `npm install`, so check the result afterwards with `aiskills installed`.

### No telemetry

`npx skills` sends anonymous usage data to `skills.sh` unless `DISABLE_TELEMETRY` or `DO_NOT_TRACK` is set. `aiskills` passes both through:

```bash
DO_NOT_TRACK=1 aiskills install -G scrolls -a claude-code
```

### External skills

Prefer `owner/repo@skill` over a bare name with `--route`. A bare name fails when the registry has several exact matches, and the registry can change between runs.

## Troubleshooting

- **Exit code 1 with `could not read the agent list from 'npx skills'`**: an `-a` pattern needs `npx skills`. Pass plain agent names instead of patterns.
- **The output has `npx skills` progress mixed in**: `npx skills` writes to the same terminal. Use the exit code, and `aiskills installed` afterwards.

See also: [CLI reference](../reference/cli.md) · [Errors and exit codes](../reference/errors.md) · [`llms.txt`](../llms.txt)

<!-- source: guides/choose-the-skills-cli-version.md -->
# How to choose the `skills` CLI version

Use this when you need a newer or different release of the `skills` CLI than the one `aiskills` pins.

Every `npx` call that `aiskills` makes runs one tested version of the `skills` CLI, `skills@1.7.6`, so a new release (or a compromised one) is never picked up without testing. `AISKILLS_SKILLS_VERSION` overrides it.

## Steps

1. Set the version for one command:

   <!-- verify -->
   ```bash
   AISKILLS_SKILLS_VERSION=latest aiskills skills --version
   ```

   ```text
   [aiskills] running: npx -y skills@latest --version
   ```

2. Or for every command, in your shell profile:

   ```bash
   export AISKILLS_SKILLS_VERSION=1.7.6
   ```

## Variations

Accepted values are an exact version (`1.7.6`, `1.8.0-beta.1`), `latest` or `next`. Anything else is refused before `npx` runs, so a typo can't turn into a different package:

<!-- verify -->
```bash
AISKILLS_SKILLS_VERSION='^1' aiskills find pdf
```

```text
[aiskills] AISKILLS_SKILLS_VERSION must be an exact version (e.g. 1.7.6), "latest" or "next"; got '^1'
```

## Troubleshooting

- **`-a` patterns or `--route` stop working on a newer version**: `aiskills` reads two pieces of `npx skills` text output (the "Valid agents:" list and `find` results). If a release changes them, go back to the pinned version and report it.

> [!WARNING]
> `latest` gives up the protection of the pinned version. Use it to try a release, not as a permanent setting.

See also: [`AISKILLS_SKILLS_VERSION`](../reference/environment.md#aiskills_skills_version) · [Security model](../concepts/security.md)

<!-- source: guides/leave-files-out.md -->
# How to leave files out of the package

This guide is for maintainers of the [sugatoray/aiskills](https://github.com/sugatoray/aiskills) repo: use a `.skillsignore` to keep files, folders or whole skills out of the npm package.

The package is built from the repo's `skills/` folder when it is packed. A `.skillsignore` file, in `skills/` or any folder below it, lists what to leave out, in `.gitignore` syntax.

## Steps

1. Create or edit a `.skillsignore`, for example `skills/.skillsignore`:

   ```gitignore
   # every tests/ folder, at any depth
   **/tests/
   # all .log files except keep.log
   *.log
   !keep.log
   # ignoring a skill's folder drops the whole skill
   scrolls/wip-skill/
   ```

2. Build the package contents and look at them:

   ```bash
   cd src/packages/aiskills
   npm run vendor
   ```

   What was left out is listed under `ignored` in `.aiskills/layout.json`.

3. Run the tests, which compare the package with every git-tracked file under `skills/` that no `.skillsignore` excludes, then clean up:

   ```bash
   npm test
   npm run clean
   ```

## Variations

### Rules for one folder

A `.skillsignore` deeper down applies to its own folder and below, after the outer rules. Its `!` rules can re-include files an outer rule left out.

## Troubleshooting

- **`.skillsignore ignores <group>/<skill>/SKILL.md; to drop a skill, ignore the folder (<group>/<skill>/) instead`**: ignoring only a `SKILL.md` would leave a skill without a definition. Ignore the folder.
- **A pattern with a `/` in the middle doesn't match deeper files**: like `.gitignore`, a `/` in the middle anchors the pattern to the `.skillsignore`'s folder. Write `**/meta/MAINTAINERS.md` for any depth.
- **A `#` after a pattern**: is part of the pattern. Put comments on their own lines.

See also: [`.skillsignore` reference](../reference/skillsignore.md) · [Files and schemas](../reference/files.md#aiskillslayoutjson)

<!-- source: concepts/how-it-works.md -->
# How aiskills works

`aiskills` saves the bundled skills to one folder on your machine and asks `npx skills` to install them from there; it never writes into agent folders itself.

![Architecture: the npm package syncs its skills to ~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills (1), aiskills runs npx skills add on that folder (2), and npx skills installs into the agents' skill folders (3); with --route, npx skills also finds and adds skills from the skills.sh registry and GitHub](../images/architecture.svg)

The same, as steps:

1. **Sync.** The npm package carries the skills (one folder per skill), a map of their original folders (`.aiskills/layout.json`) and the repo's `marketplace.json`. `aiskills` copies them to the **install folder**, `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills` (or `AISKILLS_HOME`), replacing `skills/` each time.
2. **Add.** It runs `npx -y skills@1.7.6 add <install folder>` with your skills, agents and scope.
3. **Install.** `npx skills` installs the skills into each agent's folder (`~/.claude/skills/`, `~/.agents/skills/`, or the project's folders with `-p`) and records where each one came from.

With `--route`, step 2 also runs `npx skills find` and `npx skills add <owner/repo@skill>` for skills that aren't bundled.

## Who owns what

| Thing | Owner | `aiskills` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The skills in the package | The package version you installed | Reads |
| `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/` | `aiskills` | Writes; `skills/` is replaced on every sync |
| Agents' skill folders | `npx skills` | Never touches |
| The record of installed skills | `npx skills` (`npx skills list --json`) | Reads, to know what it installed |

A skill counts as installed **by `aiskills`** when `npx skills list --json` reports it with `sourceType` `local` and `source` equal to the install folder. That is how a full `aiskills uninstall` removes exactly its own skills and leaves same-named skills from other sources alone.

## What a command does

![Install flow: parse options, sync the install folder, select skills, expand agent patterns, look up external skills (with --route), then npx skills add; a problem in parsing, selection, agents or lookup stops with exit code 1 before anything is installed](../images/install-flow.svg)

`aiskills install`, step by step:

1. Parse the options. `AISKILLS_*` variables give the defaults; options replace them.
2. Sync the install folder.
3. Turn `-s` and `-G` (names, aliases, patterns) into exact skill names.
4. Expand `-a` patterns against the agent list `npx skills` reports.
5. With `--route`, look up every external name.
6. Run `npx skills add` for the bundled skills, then once per external skill.

Every check and lookup in steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 runs before step 6. A problem stops the command with exit code 1 and installs nothing.

`uninstall` reads `npx skills list --json`, keeps the rows from the install folder (or any source with `--route`), matches `-s`/`-G` against them, and runs `npx skills remove`. The npm install step runs the install steps with no options, only `AISKILLS_*` variables.

## Why it works this way

- **One tool owns the agent folders.** `npx skills` already knows every agent's folder layout and keeps a record. Delegating to it keeps `aiskills` small and gives it new agents for free.
- **A local folder works offline.** After the npm install, `aiskills install` needs no network except to fetch the `skills` CLI the first time.
- **No runtime dependencies.** The package is plain Node.js.

## Trade-offs and limits

- **`npx skills` output is mixed in.** `aiskills` lets `npx skills` print to your terminal. Use exit codes and `aiskills installed` to check results.
- **Two pieces of `npx skills` text are parsed**: the "Valid agents:" list (for `-a` patterns) and `find` results (for `--route`). A new `skills` release could change them, which is one reason the version is pinned.
- **Updates come with the package.** Skills change when you install a newer `@sugatoray-ai/aiskills`.

See also: [Layouts](layouts.md) · [Security model](security.md) · [Files and schemas](../reference/files.md)

<!-- source: concepts/skill-groups.md -->
# Skill groups

A skill group is a named set of related skills, taken from the repo's `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`; `-G` installs or removes a whole group at once.

## Where groups come from

The package bundles the repo's `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` (the Claude Code plugin marketplace file) and saves it to the install folder. `aiskills` reads it only to group the skills. Nothing is installed as a Claude Code plugin.

| Part | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- |
| **Group name** | An entry's `name` under `plugins`, exactly as written, e.g. `scrolls-skills`. |
| **Skills in the group** | Every skill whose original folder in the repo is under the entry's `source` (relative to `metadata.pluginRoot`, `./skills`). |
| **Alias** | Not in the file. `aiskills` removes a trailing `-skills`: `scrolls-skills` → `scrolls`. A name without `-skills` is its own alias. |
| **`all`** | Not in the file. A built-in group with every bundled skill, grouped or not. `-G '*'` is the same. |

Entries whose `source` isn't a local folder (a git URL, say) are skipped, because their skills aren't in the package.

## The groups in this version

| Group | Alias | Skills |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scrolls-skills` | `scrolls` | scrolls-help, scrolls-hide, scrolls-remove, scrolls-restore, scrolls-setup, scrolls-unhide, scrolls-update |
| `stata-skills` | `stata` | stata-recipes |
| `repo-related-skills` | `repo-related` | create-issues-update-pr |
| `docs-skills` | `docs` | create-lib-docs |
| `diagrams-skills` | `diagrams` | network-flow |
| `personas-skills` | `personas` | prodigy |
| `all` (built in) | | all 13 skills |

`newsletter-ai` is in no group. Install it with `-s newsletter-ai` or `-G all`. `aiskills groups` always shows the list for the version you have.

## How names are matched

- Name or alias, in any letter case: `scrolls-skills`, `scrolls` and `Scrolls` are the same group.
- Patterns match both the name and the alias: `-G 'd*'` selects `docs-skills` and `diagrams-skills`.
- A name or pattern that matches no group stops the command and lists the valid ones.
- `-G` and `-s` add up: you get the union.

## Why membership uses the original folders

The install folder can be [flat or nested](layouts.md). Group membership is worked out from each skill's original folder, recorded in `.aiskills/layout.json`, so a group has the same skills in either layout.

## Adding a group

For maintainers: add a `plugins` entry to the repo's `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` whose `source` is a folder under `skills/`, and publish a new package version. No code changes.

See also: [`groups`](../reference/cli.md#groups) · [`-G`, `--group`](../reference/cli.md#-g---group---groups) · [1. Install a group](../tutorial/01-install-a-group.md)

<!-- source: concepts/layouts.md -->
# Layouts: flat and nested

The install folder's `skills/` can be written flat (one folder per skill, the default) or nested (the repo's own folders); agents get the same skills either way.

![Two layouts: --flat writes skills/<skill>/ for every skill; --nested writes the repo's skills/<group>/<skill>/ folders, with group files such as README.md](../images/layouts.svg)

| Layout | `skills/` looks like | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flat` (default) | `skills/scrolls-setup/SKILL.md`, `skills/prodigy/SKILL.md`, … | You just want the skills |
| `nested` | `skills/scrolls/scrolls-setup/SKILL.md`, `skills/scrolls/README.md`, `skills/personas/prodigy/SKILL.md`, … | You browse or edit the skills, or a tool expects the repo's layout |

## How the choice is made

The first of these that is set wins:

1. `--flat` or `--nested` on the command line;
2. `AISKILLS_LAYOUT` (`flat` or `nested`);
3. the layout of the last sync, saved as `layout` in `aiskills.json`;
4. `flat`.

So a choice is remembered until you pass the other flag.

## Why the package ships flat

- `npx skills experimental_sync` finds skills in a `node_modules` package only one level deep, at `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. Shipping flat makes the package work with it. See [the guide](../guides/use-experimental-sync.md).
- Each folder is named after the skill's `name:`, so names are unique and easy to find.

## How nested is rebuilt

The package also carries `.aiskills/layout.json` (each skill's original folder, e.g. `scrolls-setup` → `scrolls/scrolls-setup`) and `.aiskills/nested/` (every file outside a skill folder, such as group READMEs and `plugin.json` files). `--nested` puts the skills back in their original folders and adds those files, which gives the repo's `skills/` folder byte for byte, minus anything a `.skillsignore` left out.

npm drops files named `.gitignore` and `.npmignore` from packages, so the package stores them as `_gitignore` and `_npmignore`, and every sync renames them back.

## Trade-offs and limits

- Every sync replaces `skills/` completely. Don't keep your own files there.
- The layout changes only the install folder. Agent folders get the same skills, named the same way.

See also: [Keep the repo's nested layout](../guides/keep-the-nested-layout.md) · [`--nested`](../reference/cli.md#--nested) · [`AISKILLS_LAYOUT`](../reference/environment.md#aiskills_layout)

<!-- source: concepts/bundled-and-external.md -->
# Bundled and external skills

Bundled skills ship in this package; external skills come from anywhere else, and `aiskills` manages them only when you add `--route` (or use `aix`).

## The difference

| | Bundled | External |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Where it comes from | This package, via `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills` | The skills.sh registry, GitHub, a URL or a path |
| Installed by | `npx skills add <install folder> --skill <name>` | `npx skills add <owner/repo@skill>` |
| Needs `--route` | No | Yes |
| Shown by `installed` | Yes | Only with `--route` |
| Removed by a full `uninstall` | Yes | Never; name it with `--route` |

## What `--route` changes

**install.** Each `-s` entry that isn't bundled is handed to `npx skills`:

| `-s` entry | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| A bundled name or a pattern | Installed from the install folder, as without `--route`. Patterns only match bundled skills. |
| A bare name that isn't bundled, e.g. `pdf` | `npx skills find pdf`; installed only if exactly one result is named exactly `pdf`. |
| `owner/repo@skill` | `npx skills add owner/repo@skill`, no lookup. |
| `owner/repo`, a URL or a path | `npx skills add <spec>`, which installs the skills found there. |

**uninstall.** Names and patterns also match skills from other sources. `owner/repo@skill` is reduced to `skill`; a bare `owner/repo` is refused because it names no skill. Names that aren't installed are skipped with a warning. A full uninstall still removes only bundled skills.

**installed.** Lists every skill in the scope, with a source column: `bundled`, or the source `npx skills` recorded.

## Why a bare name needs exactly one match

The registry is shared and changes. If two repositories both publish a skill called `pdf`, picking one would be a guess about which code you trust. `aiskills` stops and lists the candidates so you can choose with `owner/repo@skill`. It also ignores results whose `owner/repo@skill` contains anything but letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`.

## Trade-offs and limits

- `npx skills remove` removes by name, so `--route uninstall -s pdf` removes `pdf` whichever source it came from.
- External skills aren't copied into the install folder, and `--purge` doesn't remove them.
- Lookups need network access to `skills.sh`.

See also: [4. Add external skills](../tutorial/04-add-external-skills.md) · [`--route`](../reference/cli.md#--route) · [Security model](security.md)

<!-- source: concepts/security.md -->
# Security model

`aiskills` writes only to its install folder, starts only a pinned `npx skills`, and checks anything from the registry before using it; the skills themselves are code your agent may run.

The full policy, including how to report a vulnerability, is in the package's [SECURITY.md](../../../SECURITY.md). This page explains the model.

## What it touches

| What | When |
| --- | --- |
| `~/.config/sugatoray/aiskills/` (or `AISKILLS_HOME`) | Written by the npm install step, `install`, `sync`, `list` and `groups`. `skills/` is replaced each time. `--purge` deletes the folder. |
| Agents' skill folders | Only through `npx skills add` / `remove`. |
| An empty temporary folder | While reading the agent list for `-a` patterns; deleted straight after. |
| The network | Never directly. `npx` downloads the `skills` CLI; `npx skills` talks to `skills.sh` and GitHub. |

## Protections

Each one is covered by the test suite.

- **Pinned `skills` CLI.** Every call is `npx -y skills@1.7.6 ...`, so a new or compromised release isn't used until it has been tested. [`AISKILLS_SKILLS_VERSION`](../reference/environment.md#aiskills_skills_version) overrides it, and only accepts an exact version, `latest` or `next`.
- **Registry results are checked.** With `--route`, a `find` result is used only if its `owner/repo@skill` is made of letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, and a bare name needs exactly one exact match.
- **No shell syntax on Windows.** `npx.cmd` runs through `cmd.exe`, so `aiskills` refuses arguments containing `& | < > ^ % ! " ( )`.
- **Only its own folders are replaced or deleted.** `sync`, `install` and `uninstall --purge` refuse a folder that has other files but no `aiskills.json`. This guards against an `AISKILLS_HOME` pointed at the wrong place.
- **npm's own variables are removed** before `npx` runs (registry, proxy and certificate settings are kept).
- **No runtime dependencies.**

## Skills are code
